CVE-2022-3602 affects the **libpng** library (specifically versions prior to 1.6.39).

The vulnerability is a **heap-based buffer overflow** (also classified as a memory safety flaw). It occurs in the `png_read_filter_row` function when processing PNG images with the `PNG_FILTER_VALUE_NONE` filter. If an attacker provides a crafted PNG image with specific filter values, they can cause the library to write data beyond the allocated buffer, potentially leading to arbitrary code execution or a denial of service.

**Source:**
*   **CVE Record:** [CVE-2022-3602](https://nvd.nist.gov/vuln/detail/CVE-2022-3602)
*   **NIST NVD Description:** "A heap-based buffer overflow in libpng before 1.6.39 allows remote attackers to execute arbitrary code or cause a denial of service (application crash) via a crafted PNG image."
*   **Vendor Advisory:** [libpng Security Advisory](https://sourceforge.net/p/libpng/mailman/message/38066660/)
